segments: ... and the kings led them away and they went (and turned aside). {OCR?}
The Franks gained dominion at this time from Mardin and Shabakhtan as far as al-Arish on the border of Egypt.
And there was nothing left for the Arabs in all Syria,
except for Aleppo, Hamat, Homs, and Damascus, while paying tribute.
For from the region of Aleppo they used to take half of the produce,
even from the mill that was at the gate of Aleppo which is called the Gate of the Gardens.
And to all the Christian slaves who were in Damascus, they sent envoys and counted them;
and whoever did not wish to live with the Arabs,
they would take from his masters freely without price.
And their raiding parties reached as far as Amid, Nisibis, and Resh'aina;
and the people of Callinicus (Raqqa) and Harran were brought to utter humiliation by them;
and only with difficulty were the Arabs able to travel from the east to Damascus by the desert road.
And in this year, which is the year 1441
of the Greeks [1129/1130 AD], Thoros, the ruler of Cilicia, died,
and Leo his brother succeeded him.
And Bohemond the Frank, the lord of Antioch, stirred up conflict with Leo.
And on the eighth of Adar of this year,
which is the year 524
of the Arabs [1130 AD],
there was a severe earthquake in Baghdad,
and it destroyed many houses.
And in Mosul a great cloud arose, and there was a violent tempest;
then coals of fire came down from the ether to the earth,
and burned many houses along with their possessions.
And this was a fearful and terrible portent.
And in this year, a Byzantine satrap named Kasianos (Cassianus?) defected to Amir Ghazi, the son of Danishmend,
and surrendered to him many fortresses in the region of Pontus.
And he gained dominion over all Cappadocia,
and gathered a large army,
and entered Cilicia to plunder.
And it happened that on that same day, Bohemond, the lord of Antioch, also entered from the other side,
without being aware of one another.
Immediately, the Turks and the Franks encountered each other,
while Leo the Armenian kept clear of battle with both of them.
And the Turks defeated the Franks,
and killed Bohemond,
because they did not know that he was the king.
Leo, however, seized the mountain passes from {OCR?} the Turks,
and put many of them to the sword.
And in the year 525
of the Arabs [1130/1131 AD],
the lord of Damascus imprisoned Dubais the Mazyadid,
and handed him over to Zengi.
